reasons: Section 13.4.1 grants both Parties, including AbbVie (our side), an express right to assign without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, stock sale or asset sale, with all other assignments subject to consent that may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed — this meets the fallback (mutual successor assignment plus reasonableness standard) and is well clear of the walk-away (no blanket bar on Customer assignment).

The change-of-control machinery in Section 13.2 runs only against Harpoon (notice of a Change in Control of Harpoon) and confers no Vendor termination or re-pricing right on a Customer change of control, so the key ASSIGN risk trigger is absent.

Consistent with a compliant classification, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed and the rendered text is unchanged; the rationale correctly relegates the preferred-only gaps (no bar on Harpoon assigning to an AbbVie competitor; mutual rather than one-way restriction) to notes rather than deviations.
Deterministic check confirms the successor/affiliate carve-out for Customer is present; nothing in the cited paragraphs contradicts the compliance conclusion.
